links.mechanism:
Every cross-service link or redirect is an ABSOLUTE URL built on the server from the TARGET service's base URL, held in the SOURCE service's convict config (src/config/config.js). Each one is documented as browser-visible: the trader's browser follows it, so it must resolve outside the Docker network.

Config keys on main today:

| Source service | Config key | Env var | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| INS frontend | tradeImportsAnimalsFrontend.baseUrl | TRADE_IMPORTS_ANIMALS_FRONTEND_URL | http://localhost:3000 |
| INS frontend | tradeImportsPlantsFrontend.baseUrl | TRADE_IMPORTS_PLANTS_FRONTEND_URL | http://localhost:3003 |
| Animals frontend | tradeImportsInsFrontend.baseUrl | TRADE_IMPORTS_INS_FRONTEND_URL | http://localhost:3002 |
| Plants frontend | tradeImportsInsFrontend.baseUrl | TRADE_IMPORTS_INS_FRONTEND_URL | http://localhost:3002 |

How a URL is built: base URL with any trailing slash removed, then the set base, then the path. INS does this in one helper, buildSetBaseUrl(configKey, setBase) in src/server/common/helpers/set-base-url.js, with set bases from src/server/common/constants/journey-set-bases.js. Today that file holds only LIVE_ANIMALS '/live-animals'; the stale branch added '/germinal-products' and '/high-risk-plants'. Animals and plants do the same join inline: `config.get('tradeImportsInsFrontend.baseUrl').replace(/\/$/, '')`.

Each frontend also exports siblingFrontendBaseUrls from its config. src/server/common/helpers/content-security-policy.js adds those origins to CSP form-action, which lets a form POST redirect to a sibling service. Chrome checks form-action at every hop of a redirect chain.

A relative path never works between services:
- **CDP:** each service is its own origin (https://trade-imports-<svc>.<env>.cdp-int.defra.cloud).
- **Local and CI stacks:** each service is its own port on localhost (3000 animals, 3002 INS, 3003 plants).

Server-to-server API calls (backends, address book, reference data) are a different class. They use host.docker.internal in the stacks and must never be reused for a browser link.

The local stack and the CI stack are the same thing. The reusable CI workflow (DEFRA/trade-imports-workspace .github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml):
- checks out the workspace at the PR's branch name if one exists, otherwise main;
- runs ./scripts/stack/run-stack.sh --branch <branch>, so it uses the same docker/stack/*.compose.yml values as a laptop;
- runs the tests image with --network host against localhost:3000/3002/3003.

So a compose change only reaches CI if the workspace has a branch with the same name, or the change is already on main.

CSP form-action across sign-in. The type question is a POST on INS that redirects to an animals or plants start entry. If the trader has no session yet on that frontend, it redirects on to the Defra ID stub, then to its own /auth/sign-in-oidc, then to the journey. Chrome checks every hop against INS's form-action, which today lists only self plus the animals and plants origins, so the stub hop is blocked. The stale branch fixed this with DEFRA_ID_FORM_ACTION_ORIGINS, but only defaulted it to localhost:3007. It never put the value in compose or cdp-app-config. Copied as it is, the fix passes locally and in CI and fails in CDP. The same chain applies to any POST on animals or plants that redirects to INS.

Deriving the stub origin from DEFRA_ID_OIDC_CONFIGURATION_URL is wrong in the stacks. That URL is host.docker.internal:3007, server-side only, while the browser sees localhost:3007. Either use an explicit browser-facing setting, or rewrite it the same way DEFRA_ID_SIGN_OUT_HOSTNAME_REWRITE_ENABLED does.

The start entries do not exist on main. Animals serves /live-animals (its dashboard) and POST /live-animals/notifications. Plants serves /high-risk-plants. Neither serves /<set>/start, and animals has no germinal-products set. A compose change only reaches CI if the workspace repo has a branch with the same name. The CI workflow checks out trade-imports-workspace at the PR's branch name, else main. Any new or changed docker/stack env var for this theme therefore needs a feat/EUDPA-690-type-question branch in the workspace too, and the theme's repo list does not include the workspace today.

@compose-only specs never prove CDP, because the CDP test scripts invert @compose. Hand-over specs must stay untagged @compose and assert by origin from TRADE_IMPORTS_*_FRONTEND_BASE_URL, so they pass on both the cdp-int hosts and localhost.

In template mode its Back link goes to the templates list with Templates highlighted in the service navigation, and choosing a type stores it on the template as a draft and goes on to the template name page instead of an origin page. Templates carry their type (9 October ruling). This is this area's part of the template-start row.

It needs saved templates to reorder, so it lands after saving a template.

rows.detail: A trader building or changing a live animals template answers Roles and addresses on the same pages as a notification. Today 'Add a new address' crosses to the INS frontend's add page with a handshake that names a notification, and the return lands on that notification's picker, so a trader adding an address while building a template would lose their place. This row makes the round trip and each role's 'Edit details' page work in template mode exactly as they do for a notification: the handshake names the template, every way back from the INS add page returns to that template's own pages with the template's answer set as it would be for a notification, and an edit changes only the template's copy of the address, never the address book record. Nothing returns the trader to a notification. The INS frontend stays the address book's only writer. Every link and redirect between the two services takes its address from each service's own configured address for the other, as the address book link and today's handshake do, so the round trip works on CDP, on the local Docker stack and on the Docker stack the pull request end-to-end runs use. Template mode is animals only, so plants is unchanged.
